title: CBSE class 10 | AI Test | Communication skill | Revisiting Ai project cycle & Ethics Frameworks for AI
description: CBSE class 10 | AI 2 Chapter Test | Communication skill | Revisiting Ai project cycle & Ethics Frameworks for AI
chapters: Revisiting Ai project cycle & Ethics Frameworks for AI
topics: Revisiting Ai project cycle & Ethics Frameworks for AI
subject: ai-artificial-intelligence

questions.question: Rahul is sending an email to his manager about a project delay. Instead of writing a 500-word essay, he uses bullet points to explain the issue in 50 words without losing the core meaning. Which of the 7Cs of effective communication is he applying?
questions.explanation: Conciseness means communicating the required message in the fewest possible words without sacrificing the other C's of communication.
questions.hint: It means getting straight to the point.

questions.question: Which of the following stages are officially part of the AI Project Cycle? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: The AI Project Cycle consists of Problem Scoping, Data Acquisition, Data Exploration, Modelling, and Evaluation. Deployment is a post-cycle phase.
questions.hint: Think of the core steps required before an AI is released to the public.

questions.question: During a virtual team meeting, Sarah cannot understand her colleague's presentation because her internet connection keeps dropping and there is construction noise outside her window. What type of communication barrier is this?
questions.explanation: Physical barriers relate to environmental factors, distance, or technical issues that prevent the clear transmission of the message.
questions.hint: The issue lies in the environment and medium, not the minds or language of the speakers.

questions.question: The 4Ws Problem Canvas is used during the Problem Scoping stage. Which of the following are included in the 4Ws? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: The 4Ws Canvas consists of Who (stakeholders), What (the problem), Where (context/situation), and Why (benefits of solving it).
questions.hint: Think about identifying the stakeholders, the issue, the location, and the reason.

questions.question: "Your performance in the last coding test was poor because you did not use the correct syntax for the loop." What type of feedback is this?
questions.explanation: Specific feedback points directly to the exact area of improvement or error, rather than giving a vague "you did poorly" statement.
questions.hint: It pinpoints exactly what went wrong.

questions.question: A company develops an AI screening tool for hiring. The tool consistently rejects resumes from female candidates because it was trained on historical data from a male-dominated tech industry. What ethical concern does this highlight?
questions.explanation: AI bias occurs when algorithms reflect human biases present in the training data, leading to unfair or discriminatory outcomes.
questions.hint: The model is acting with prejudice based on historical imbalances.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences correctly demonstrate the use of a subordinating conjunction? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Although he was tired, he finished the project.
I wanted to go, but it started raining.
She will call you when she arrives at the station.
You can have tea or you can have coffee.

questions.explanation: "Although" and "when" are subordinating conjunctions that introduce dependent clauses. "But" and "or" are coordinating conjunctions.
questions.hint: Look for words that make a clause dependent on the main sentence.

questions.question: In an AI project for predicting weather, the team collects 10 years of temperature data, satellite images, and wind speeds. They decide to visualize this data using graphs to find trends. Which stage of the AI cycle are they currently in?
questions.explanation: Data Exploration involves visualizing and analyzing the acquired data to find patterns, trends, and relationships before feeding it to a model.
questions.hint: They already have the data; now they are trying to "understand" it visually.

questions.question: Which of the following non-verbal cues contribute to positive body language during a professional presentation? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Maintaining steady eye contact with the audience
Using open hand gestures while explaining
Crossing arms tightly across the chest

questions.explanation: Eye contact and open gestures project confidence and engagement. Crossed arms suggest defensiveness, and fidgeting indicates nervousness.
questions.hint: Think about cues that make you appear approachable and confident.

questions.question: If an AI model is designed purely based on fixed logical conditions (IF-THEN-ELSE statements) provided by a human expert, what type of model is it?
questions.explanation: In a rule-based approach, the AI follows pre-defined logical rules explicitly programmed by the developer. It does not learn from data.
questions.hint: The machine is following strict instructions rather than finding its own patterns.

questions.question: Which part of speech modifies a verb, an adjective, or another adverb, often ending in "-ly"?
questions.explanation: Adverbs provide more context about how, when, or where an action occurs (e.g., quickly, very).
questions.hint: It "adds" to the meaning of a verb.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid domains of Artificial Intelligence? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: The three core domains of AI covered in the syllabus are Data Sciences, Computer Vision, and Natural Language Processing. Cloud computing is an infrastructure technology, not an AI domain.
questions.hint: Think about how AI processes numbers, images, and text.

questions.question: In the communication cycle, what is the process of interpreting the message by the receiver called?
questions.explanation: Decoding is the mental process where the receiver translates the sender's message (words/symbols) into understandable meaning.
questions.hint: It is the opposite of what the sender does to construct the message.

questions.question: An AI healthcare application asks users for their medical history. To maintain ethical standards regarding Data Privacy, what MUST the application do? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Obtain explicit consent from the user before collecting data
Sell the data to third-party advertisers for targeted ads
Anonymize the data so individual patients cannot be identified
Store the data indefinitely without user permission

questions.explanation: Data privacy requires informed consent and the protection of user identity (anonymization). Misusing or endlessly storing data violates these ethical principles.
questions.hint: Think about how you would want a hospital to handle your medical records.

questions.question: Identify the type of sentence: "Please close the door when you leave."
questions.explanation: Imperative sentences give commands, requests, or instructions.
questions.hint: It is telling someone to do something.

questions.question: In the 4Ws Problem Canvas, which block specifically defines the context or the situation in which the stakeholders face the problem?
questions.explanation: The 'Where' block details the context, environment, or location where the problem arises.
questions.hint: It answers the question of "location" or "scenario".

questions.question: Effective feedback should ideally be: (Select all that apply)

options.text: Delayed for several months to allow reflection
Given with a positive and constructive intent
Based on personal attacks rather than actions

questions.explanation: Good feedback is timely, specific, and focuses on behavior and improvement (constructive) rather than personal traits.
questions.hint: How would you want a teacher to grade your project so you can improve?

questions.question: An AI system is built to scan crowded airports and instantly identify individuals on a security watchlist. Which AI domain is heavily utilized here?
questions.explanation: Computer Vision enables machines to derive meaningful information from digital images, videos, and other visual inputs (like facial recognition).
questions.hint: The AI relies on seeing and analyzing visuals.

questions.question: "The boy ran fast to catch the bus, but he missed it." What is the article in this sentence?
questions.explanation: "The" is a definite article used before the nouns "boy" and "bus" to specify them.
questions.hint: Look for words like a, an, or the.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the "Evaluation" phase of the AI project cycle are true? (Select all that apply)

options.text: It involves testing the model against testing data to check its accuracy.
It is the phase where we collect data from sensors.
It helps determine if the model is ready for real-world deployment.

questions.explanation: Evaluation is the testing phase to check model reliability and accuracy. Data collection happens in Acquisition, and the 4Ws are in Problem Scoping.
questions.hint: Think of this as the "final exam" for the AI model.

questions.question: When a communicator respects the receiver's feelings, background, and viewpoint, which of the 7Cs are they demonstrating?
questions.explanation: Consideration (or "you" attitude) means stepping into the shoes of the receiver and showing empathy and respect for their context.
questions.hint: It involves thinking about the other person.

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios represent a breach of "Accountability" in AI Ethics? (Select all that apply)

options.text: An autonomous vehicle crashes, and neither the manufacturer nor the software developer takes responsibility.
An AI recommends a movie, and the user doesn't like it.
A medical AI misdiagnoses a patient, and the hospital cannot identify who is liable for the error.
An AI translates a text correctly.

questions.explanation: Accountability means it must be clear who is legally and morally responsible when an AI system causes harm or fails.
questions.hint: Who takes the blame when things go wrong?

questions.question: What is the fundamental difference between a phrase and a sentence?

options.text: A phrase always ends with a full stop.
A sentence does not have a subject.
A sentence expresses a complete thought, while a phrase does not.
A phrase contains both a subject and a predicate.

questions.explanation: A sentence has a subject and a verb and forms a complete thought. A phrase is a group of words lacking a subject-verb pairing and incomplete in meaning.
questions.hint: "In the morning" vs "I woke up in the morning".

questions.question: Siri, Alexa, and Google Assistant are prime examples of AI systems that can understand human speech and reply in human-like language. What AI domain drives this capability?
questions.explanation: NLP bridges the gap between human communication (text/speech) and computer understanding.
questions.hint: Focus on the word "Language".

questions.question: Overcoming communication barriers is essential for teamwork. Which of the following are effective ways to overcome these barriers? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Checking for understanding by asking for feedback
Assuming the receiver has understood the message

questions.explanation: Clarity, active feedback, and controlling physical environment help ensure the message is delivered and understood properly.
questions.hint: Think of actions that actively clarify a message.

questions.question: If a model continuously adapts and improves its performance based on new data without human intervention, it follows a:
questions.explanation: Learning-based models (like Machine Learning) use algorithms to parse data, learn from it, and make informed decisions, improving over time.
questions.hint: The system is "studying" data rather than following hardcoded rules.

questions.question: "The cat slept on the mat." In this sentence, what is the word "on"?
questions.explanation: A preposition shows the relationship of a noun or pronoun (the mat) to another word in the sentence (slept).
questions.hint: It indicates position or direction.

questions.question: When acquiring data for an AI project on global warming, which of the following sources would be considered reliable and ethical? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Open-source datasets provided by government meteorological departments
Rumors and posts on unverified social media accounts
Satellite imagery published by space agencies like NASA or ISRO
Private data stolen from a competitor's server

questions.explanation: Ethical data acquisition requires using verified, authentic, and legally obtained sources.
questions.hint: Look for official and legal sources of information.

questions.question: Why is "Clarity" crucial in written communication?

options.text: It makes the document look visually appealing.
It ensures the reader grasps the exact meaning without confusion.
It proves the writer has a large vocabulary.
It guarantees the reader will agree with the writer.

questions.explanation: Clarity ensures the message is straightforward and easy to comprehend, avoiding ambiguity.
questions.hint: It prevents misunderstandings.

questions.question: The AI project cycle is highly iterative. What does "iterative" mean in this context?

options.text: The steps must be followed exactly once in a linear path.
The cycle can loop back to earlier stages to refine the model based on testing and new data.
It requires multiple teams to work on the same problem.
The project is impossible to finish.

questions.explanation: Iterative means repetitive and cyclical; if a model fails evaluation, the team can loop back to data acquisition or modelling to improve it.
questions.hint: Think of a circle rather than a straight line.

questions.question: Which of the following demonstrate internal self-motivation as a psychological factor in overcoming communication barriers? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Actively controlling one's anger before sending an email
Ignoring someone because you don't like their accent
Rephrasing your sentence calmly when someone misunderstands you
Blaming the other person for not understanding

questions.explanation: Self-regulation and motivation help a communicator overcome internal psychological barriers like frustration or bias.
questions.hint: Focus on positive internal control.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the 'Why' block in the Problem Scoping canvas?

options.text: To decide which programming language to use.
To identify who is facing the problem.
To determine the value and benefits of solving the problem.

questions.explanation: The 'Why' block justifies the project by defining the solution's impact and benefits to the stakeholders.
questions.hint: It answers the question: "Why do we care?"

questions.question: Identify the correct order of a basic paragraph structure.

options.text: Topic Sentence -> Supporting Details -> Concluding Sentence
Concluding Sentence -> Topic Sentence -> Supporting Details
Supporting Details -> Concluding Sentence -> Topic Sentence
Topic Sentence -> Concluding Sentence -> Supporting Details

questions.explanation: A well-structured paragraph introduces the main idea (topic), elaborates on it (supporting details), and wraps it up (conclusion).
questions.hint: Think of a hamburger: bun on top, meat in middle, bun on bottom.

questions.question: Which of the following are examples of unstructured data used in Data Sciences? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Audio recordings from customer service calls
A perfectly formatted Excel sheet with names and ages
Raw text from millions of tweets
A folder full of random photographs

questions.explanation: Unstructured data does not follow a predefined data model or schema, unlike tables or spreadsheets.
questions.hint: Think of data that cannot be easily put into neat rows and columns.

questions.question: The sentence "Wow, that is a beautiful painting!" is an example of which type of sentence?
questions.explanation: Exclamatory sentences express strong emotion or surprise and end with an exclamation mark.
questions.hint: Notice the punctuation at the end.

questions.question: Which ethical framework ensures that an AI system can explain HOW it arrived at a certain decision (e.g., why a loan was denied)?
questions.explanation: Transparency (or Explainable AI) ensures that the decision-making process of the algorithm is understandable to humans, not just a "black box".
questions.hint: It means being able to "see through" the model's logic.

questions.question: A sender is preparing a message. According to the principle of "Completeness" (7Cs), what must the sender ensure? (Select all that apply)

options.text: All relevant facts and figures are included.
It answers all questions asked by the receiver.
It includes unnecessary rumors to make it interesting.
It is extremely long, regardless of relevance.

questions.explanation: Completeness means providing all necessary information required by the audience to make an informed decision or understand the context.
questions.hint: Do not leave out crucial details.

questions.question: Which AI domain relies heavily on statistical algorithms, probability, and pattern recognition to analyze numerical trends?
questions.explanation: Data Sciences deals primarily with extracting insights from large volumes of data using statistics and machine learning.
questions.hint: It is all about the numbers and statistics.

questions.question: What is "Feedback" in the context of the Communication Cycle?

options.text: The medium through which the message travels.
The receiver's response or reaction to the sender's message.
The noise that interrupts the message.
The initial idea generated by the sender.

questions.explanation: Feedback completes the communication cycle by letting the sender know the message was received and understood.
questions.hint: It is the reply.

questions.question: AI Inclusion implies that technology should be accessible to everyone. Which of the following AI applications demonstrate Inclusion? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Text-to-speech software for visually impaired students.
Real-time translation apps breaking down language barriers.
High-cost AI that only elite corporations can afford.
Voice-controlled smart homes for physically disabled individuals.

questions.explanation: Inclusion ensures that AI empowers all segments of society, especially marginalized or disabled groups, rather than excluding them.
questions.hint: Think about technology making the world fairer for everyone.

questions.question: In the 4Ws Problem Canvas, which block is used to define the nature of the problem itself and how it affects the stakeholders?
questions.explanation: The 'What' block focuses on identifying the actual problem, its evidence, and how it directly impacts the stakeholders.
questions.hint: It answers the question regarding the core issue being faced.

questions.question: "Rohan and Amit are working on a machine learning project, and they need more time to finish it." Which part of speech is the word "they"?
questions.explanation: "They" is a pronoun used to replace the nouns "Rohan and Amit" to avoid repetition in the sentence.
questions.hint: It takes the place of a noun.

questions.question: A retail company wants to analyze ten years of customer purchase history to predict which products will sell best during the upcoming holiday season. Which AI domain is best suited for this task?
questions.explanation: Analyzing large sets of historical numerical and categorical data to find trends and make future predictions is the core function of Data Sciences.
questions.hint: The task heavily relies on numbers, statistics, and past trends.

questions.question: Instead of saying "Our sales improved recently," a manager states, "Our sales in the northern region increased by 15% in Q3." Which principle of effective communication is the manager applying?
questions.explanation: Concreteness means being specific, definite, and vivid rather than vague. Using exact facts and figures demonstrates this principle perfectly.
questions.hint: It leaves no room for guessing by providing exact numbers.

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios illustrate the ethical concern of "AI Bias"? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A loan approval algorithm consistently denies applications from specific neighborhoods due to historical redlining data.
An AI voice assistant struggles to understand a user due to loud background noise.
A facial recognition system has a significantly higher error rate when identifying people with darker skin tones.
A weather prediction AI incorrectly forecasts rain due to a physically broken temperature sensor.

questions.explanation: AI Bias occurs when human prejudices or unbalanced training data lead the system to make unfair, discriminatory decisions based on demographics like race, gender, or location.
questions.hint: Look for scenarios where the AI is treating certain groups of people unfairly based on historical data.

questions.question: A software engineer is explaining a server crash to the marketing team using complex terms like "TCP/IP handshake failure" and "DNS propagation delay." The marketing team is completely confused. What kind of communication barrier is this?
questions.explanation: Using heavy technical jargon with an audience that does not share that specific vocabulary creates a linguistic (or semantic) barrier.
questions.hint: The issue is rooted in the choice of words and technical vocabulary.

questions.question: During the Data Acquisition and Modelling stages, how should a developer handle the collected dataset to ensure the model is evaluated properly? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Use the entire dataset only for training the model to maximize learning.
Split the dataset into two distinct parts: Training Data and Testing Data.
Ensure the testing data is kept completely hidden from the model during the training phase.
Use the testing data to train the model if the training data is not large enough.

questions.explanation: A dataset must be split. The model learns from the Training Data, and its performance is evaluated on unseen Testing Data to ensure it can generalize and hasn't just memorized the answers.
questions.hint: Think about how a student prepares for an exam (practice) versus taking the actual unseen exam (testing).

questions.question: Identify the type of sentence: "Have you submitted the final AI project report to the teacher yet?"
questions.explanation: Interrogative sentences ask a direct question and always end with a question mark.
questions.hint: It requires an answer from the listener.

questions.question: An AI system is designed to play a complex video game. Instead of being given exact instructions on how to move, it plays millions of matches against itself, learning from its wins and losses to develop new, unprogrammed strategies. What type of approach is this?
questions.explanation: The system is learning from experience (data/gameplay) and improving its own performance without explicit human programming for every possible scenario, which defines a learning-based approach.
questions.hint: The system is figuring out the rules on its own through trial and error.

questions.question: When establishing Ethical Frameworks for AI, which of the following are considered primary goals? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Ensuring AI systems do not infringe on fundamental human rights or privacy.
Making sure AI algorithms are transparent and their decision-making processes can be explained.
Guaranteeing that AI completely replaces human decision-making in all professional fields.
Preventing algorithms from amplifying existing societal inequalities.

questions.explanation: AI ethics aims to align technology with human values, ensuring fairness, transparency, privacy, and the prevention of harm. It does not aim to blindly replace all human judgment.
questions.hint: Think about principles that protect human well-being, fairness, and safety.
